definitions.explanation: A point where something is interrupted or divided, either in time or in a continuous sequence.
A physical line or opening where something has been cut or separated.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}の{切|き}れ{目|め}に{休憩|きゅうけい}を{取|と}る。
examples.english: To take a break during a pause in work.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{切|き}れ{目|め}を{見計|みはか}らって{外|そと}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: I waited for a break in the rain and went outside.

examples.japanese: {袋|ふくろ}に{切|き}れ{目|め}を{入|い}れる。
examples.english: To make a cut in a bag.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}の{切|き}れ{目|め}に{沿|そ}って{折|お}る。
examples.english: To fold along the cut line on the paper.

examples.japanese: {壁|かべ}に{細|ほそ}い{切|き}れ{目|め}が{入|はい}っていた。
examples.english: There was a thin crack in the wall.

notes:
A compound noun from {切|き}れる (to cut/break) + {目|め} (point/spot). Refers to any point of division or interruption, whether abstract (time, conversation) or physical (a slit, crack).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {話|はなし}の{切|き}れ{目|め}: a pause in conversation
- {雨|あめ}の{切|き}れ{目|め}: a break in the rain
- {仕事|しごと}の{切|き}れ{目|め}: a break between tasks
- {切|き}れ{目|め}なく: without interruption, continuously
- {切|き}れ{目|め}を{入|い}れる: to make a cut/incision

PROVERB:
{金|かね}の{切|き}れ{目|め}が{縁|えん}の{切|き}れ{目|め}: "When the money runs out, the relationship ends" — a well-known saying about how financial problems can end relationships.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {隙間|すきま}: gap, crevice — emphasizes empty space between objects
- {区切|くぎ}り: division, punctuation — emphasizes a deliberate marking or boundary point
- {途切|とぎ}れ: break, interruption — emphasizes something stopping or being cut short
